items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: Life in the mountain is indeed carefree.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: Listen, there's the wind, the rustling leaves, and the chirping birds, all much more beautiful than that awful racket that humans make.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: Do you think so, Yànpíng?
The bird called Yànpíng moves carefully to the trunk of the tree, so he could hide in the shadow.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I've never left the mountain. Which is more annoying, the noises made by humans, or those made by animals?

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: To you, I think they would both be annoying, just in different ways.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: I admit, listening to the daily conversation of humans and their haggling in the market can sometimes be interesting.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Is that so?
Birds like any intelligent creature can have different personalities and hobbies.
One can tell the differences between them by listening carefully to their chirps. One might be loud and talkative, while the other makes only a few short sounds in reply.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: They do invent many new and useful things, some that maybe you will need one day.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: Like bricks. Our nests have been much better protected since they showed me how to make them.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: That's true.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: And the technique of making beautiful melodies with bamboo and wood with holes, or the doodles they draw that can hold their words ...

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: They can even measure time, using something they call a "calendar."

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: They can see into the essence of ordinary things and dream up wondrous creations from them.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: If you look at the world like a human does, you will probably be shocked by its vastness.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: It is.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: ... Yànpíng.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: I know you don't care about humans, but I feel I should tell you everything I want to say.
Yànpíng moves back to where he had stood before, right next to the other bird. Their wings rubbing against each other, with feathers puffing out.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: So ... you are leaving too.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Well, it's only a matter of time. Good luck.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: Thank you.
In a rare moment of silence in the tree. One of the birds stretches his wing to cover the other.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: You're still unwilling to leave the mountain ... Is it because you can't bear to stay away from home?

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I simply have not found a reason to leave.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: Your time has not yet come, I guess, but that's fine, we need someone to take care of our nests and belongings ... I'll leave my books and instruments to you.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: You are the first one born in the Central Plains after we migrated. I think you will adapt to the environment here faster than we do.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: We are so used to living high in the sky. When we look down, both the cities and the people are no different from dirt piles. Only by living among them can we truly experience the prosperity described in the poems.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: I think you will leave the mountain one day.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: But not for now, at least.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: It's not yet time for me to think of such things.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: Just as well ... You glide slowly just like always.

items.speaker: Getian's Clan Mate
items.text: Hopefully I'll be useful to our people one day. I don't want to become another lazy bone always snoozing beneath the tree ...
The seasons changed, beasts and birds came and went away. And the traces they had left behind were gone in less than a day as the leaves fell.
The stream flows downwards and the wind blows its course night and day as always.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: You've returned.

items.speaker: Bone Collector
items.text: Hmm, who ... Ah, it's you, Yànpíng.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Whose bones are these?

items.speaker: Bone Collector
items.text: Not your friends', I'm afraid.

items.speaker: Bone Collector
items.text: I will take them all to our temple. You may check them yourself should you wish.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I will.

items.speaker: Bone Collector
items.text: Quite some time has passed. Yet, still you choose not to leave the mountain.

items.speaker: Bone Collector
items.text: Well, given the situation of our race, I guess you will be the last one left to take care of our bones.

items.speaker: Bone Collector
items.text: You will have to leave one day.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I thank you for the reminder. Now, please leave me alone.
The bird robed in loose clothing stretches its wings and flies towards the point of a roof far away.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: ... It is fine weather for a nap.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Both the mountain and the human world are between the sky and the earth. Are they really different?

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Anyway, the breeze feels comfortable now. I should take a nap.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: There are so many bones left in the temple. It could take a hundred years or even more to read through each one's stories.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I might have a long life, but I'd still rather spend that time on the things I'm actually interested in.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: These stories have nothing to do with me.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: There is no need for me to leave the mountain.
The beasts in the mountain remained there for several generations, until the rocks in the stream had been polished smooth.
But the scholar tree where the birds rested remained as green as ever.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Our kind has not had a new generation for a long time.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I don't think anyone will be able to collect my bones and move them to the temple if I die outside this mountain.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: In that case, then the tombs here would eventually be buried by weeds.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: We migrated and followed the humans. We studied from different cultures. We put so much effort into prolonging the lives of our people.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Yet it was all in vain, as I expected.
What eventually led him to leave the mountain was a summoning. In layman's terms, it was like a wordless awareness or calling.
Every member of his race would have felt it. Whenever it happened, they each would fold their wings and lower their heads, and the bone collector would set off to where the bones lay.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Better make it quick.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: It's not far. Good, it's not too close to the human city. I won't be interrupted.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: He must have been on his way back to the mountain ... but didn't make it.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: No matter. I'll take him back.
From his view high in the sky, spotting the white bones strewn across the green foliage was a simple matter.
Seeing his target, he folded his wings and landed.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: We meet again.
He examined the skull beneath the cloth, and felt for a second it peered back at him. The wilderness was silent, as if the place were long abandoned.
Like how they used to, he kept a bit of a distance, but this time the bones did not hop forward to meet him.
One wing covered the other again.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: You know, I often wondered why every bone collector would eventually leave the mountain, just as you did. Was it the scenery, the people ... something else?

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: You left to help humans build cities and bridges. You even sought out water sources and gave them your so-called advice.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: What is your purpose?
There was no reply. He hadn't cast the arcane skill that might allow the skull to speak.
Yànpíng lowered his head and found a line of ants climbing through a hole in the skull.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: To verify that you have learned the right knowledge? To offer help to the creatures similar to you?

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Or you just simply could not resist the desire to do so?
Yànpíng stayed there with the silent bones for a long time. Before he took wing again.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: No matter.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: "All men, whether great or ordinary, will end up a pile of bones." There's nothing else I can say.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: It's time to return.
